foods.name: Litti Chokha
foods.description: The soul food of Bihar — wheat balls stuffed with roasted gram flour (sattu), spices, and mustard oil, baked over coal fire and served with mashed roasted brinjal and tomato. A hearty, rustic delight that defines Bihari cuisine.
foods.where: Available at every dhaba and street stall in Bhabhua

foods.name: Sattu Sharbat
foods.description: A refreshing summer drink made from roasted gram flour (sattu) mixed with water, lemon, and spices. This nutritious beverage is a staple of Bihari summers and a perfect energy booster for travelers exploring the Kaimur hills.
foods.where: Roadside stalls and local homes throughout Kaimur

foods.name: Thekua
foods.description: A crispy, sweet snack made from wheat flour, jaggery, and ghee, deep-fried to golden perfection. Thekua is an essential offering during Chhath Puja and is enjoyed as a festive treat throughout the year. Its distinctive pressed pattern makes it instantly recognizable.
foods.where: Sweet shops and homes, especially during Chhath Puja season

tips.tip: Try litti chokha at a roadside coal-fire dhaba for the most authentic experience.
Sattu sharbat is best enjoyed chilled — ask for it with black salt and lemon.
Thekua is widely available during Chhath Puja (Oct–Nov) in every household.
Most local eateries are vegetarian — ideal for plant-based travelers.
Carry cash — most street food stalls don't accept digital payments.
Meal budget: ₹100–₹200 per person at local dhabas.
